recent_videos.description:
✨ BEGINNER SKINCARE ROUTINE FOR ACNE-PRONE SKIN

☀️ MORNING ROUTINE

1. Gentle face wash
2. 5% Niacinamide serum
3. Moisturiser
4. Sunscreen SPF 30–50

🌙 NIGHT ROUTINE

Salicylic Acid Nights (Start 1–2 times a week)

1. Gentle face wash
2. Salicylic acid serum (apply as directed)
3. Moisturiser

Other Nights

1. Gentle face wash
2. Niacinamide serum (optional)
3. Moisturiser

🤍 IMPORTANT TIPS
• Start with 5% niacinamide and introduce one serum at a time.
• Don’t use salicylic acid every night when you’re a beginner.
• Avoid combining salicylic acid with other exfoliating acids or retinol initially.
• If you experience burning, redness, or peeling, stop the active products and use only a gentle cleanser, moisturiser, and sunscreen until your skin settles.
• Patch-test new products before applying them to your face.

✨ REMEMBER: These serums may help manage acne, oiliness, and clogged pores, but they cannot guarantee completely clear skin. Consistency and a healthy skin barrier matter!

recent_videos.description:
MY CURLY HAIR RESET ROUTINE | From Dry & Frizzy to Defined Curls!MY CURL RESET ROUTINE, STEP BY STEP:

1. Overnight Hair Oiling (Champi) 
I started by applying Nidhi’s Grandma Secret Hair Oil to my scalp and cold-pressed coconut oil generously along my hair lengths. I massaged my scalp well, followed by 15 minutes of heat treatment using a heat cap. Once done, I gently detangled my hair with a detangling comb, braided it, and left the oils on overnight ​⁠ . @grandmaasecret 

2. Clarifying Shampoo 
The next morning, I washed my hair with a strong clarifying shampoo to remove all the oil, dirt, and buildup. Make sure you cleanse your scalp and hair thoroughly so no oily residue is left behind before moving on to the next step. 

3. Bond Repair Hair Mask 
After shampooing, I applied a bond repair hair mask to my hair lengths, making sure to avoid my scalp. I left it on for 30 minutes, including 20 minutes of heat treatment, to give my curls some extra care. ​⁠ @letscurlupdotcom 

4. Leave-In Conditioner 
After rinsing off the mask, I applied a lightweight leave-in conditioner generously to my hair lengths. I used a wide-tooth comb to distribute the product evenly through my hair. ​⁠ 

5. Brush Styling & Gel 
Next, I brush-styled my curls using my curl styling brush and scrunched in a gel to help define my curls and hold their shape.

6. Drying & Diffusing 
I let my hair air-dry for around 10–20 minutes before using a diffuser to finish drying my curls and reveal the final results!

❤️SAVE THIS ROUTINE for the days when your curls need a little extra TLC!

Remember, this is an occasional reset routine for when my hair feels extra dry and needs more care, not something I do every wash day.

Curly Hair Products & Accessories I Carried for My 10-Day Vacation and Why

1. Manetain Moisturising Shampoo: Not as mild as a gentle shampoo or as strong as a clarifying shampoo, it effectively cleaned my scalp and removed the oils and serums I applied to my scalp and hair lengths. @manetainofficial

recent_videos.description:
The Biggest Scam in Shark Tank History? 

What started as a revolutionary invention turned into one of the most controversial stories associated with Shark Tank! Charles Michael Yim introduced Breathometer, a small device that connected to a smartphone and claimed to measure a person's blood alcohol level through their breath. Impressed by the idea, all five Sharks invested a combined $1 million in exchange for 30% equity.

But things took a shocking turn when the product's accuracy came under scrutiny. The company faced regulatory action after its alcohol readings were found to be unreliable, raising serious concerns about the product's claims and the trust investors had placed in it.

From a million-dollar investment to a major business controversy, the Breathometer story is a powerful reminder that a brilliant pitch doesn't always mean a reliable product.

recent_videos.title: Combination Skin Morning and Night skincare routine for Winters
recent_videos.description:
MORNING and Night Skincare routine for combination skin-

In the morning, use a gentle foaming cleanser that removes excess oil without making the dry areas feel tight. 

Step 2- An oil balancing and hydrating serum.
For combination skin, you can use niacinamide to help control excess oil and HA to support the skin barrier. 

Step 3- A lightweight moisturiser.
Choose a non-comedogenic, gel or lightweight moisturiser for hydration without making your T-zone greasy. 

Step 4- Sunscreen- And this step is non-negotiable. Use a broad-spectrum SPF 50 gel based sunscreen that feels lightweight on the skin. 

NIGHT
Step 1 again: A Cleanser.
Cleanse your face properly to remove oil, dirt and sunscreen. You can also double cleanse if you wear makeup or heavy sunscreen.

Step 2- Your night-time treatment.
If you have clogged pores or frequent breakouts, you can use salicylic acid 3 nights a week. Start slowly and don't over-exfoliate.

Step 3 is a Moisturiser-
Finish with the same lightweight moisturiser, focusing a little more on the drier areas.

recent_videos.title: 3 mistakes to avoid if you are using niacinamide| Best Niacinamide Serums|
recent_videos.description:
Are you using niacinamide correctly? Learn how to avoid common mistakes to get the best results for your skin.

Niacinamide is a versatile and well-tolerated ingredient, but how you apply it matters. 

3 Mistakes to Avoid When Using Niacinamide Serum:

1. Starting with a concentration that’s too high-  If you’re a beginner or have sensitive skin, start with around 4–5% niacinamide. Higher concentrations like 10% aren’t necessarily more effective for everyone and may increase the chance of irritation.
2. Applying it on irritated or compromised skin- 5 % Niacinamide can generally be used on slightly damp skin, but if you are using 10% or more, use it on dry skin. 
3. Over-layering with strong actives- Niacinamide itself is usually well tolerated, but layering it with high-strength AHA/BHA, retinoids, or other potentially irritating actives can increase the overall irritation load. If you’re new to actives, introduce them gradually rather than using everything together.

recent_videos.title: Food Craving and Iron Deficiency Symtomps
recent_videos.description:
Are you Craving unusual things? Your body may be giving you a clue.

Ice? → Check CBC + ferritin for iron deficiency.
Raw rice? → Can be pica; check iron status, especially ferritin.
Chalk or मिट्टी? → Also pica; iron deficiency is an important cause to rule out.
Paper or other non-food items? → Consider pica and get evaluated for iron deficiency.

Are you constantly craving ice, raw rice, or soil? These unusual urges are often linked to iron deficiency and should not be ignored.

Many people experience pica symptoms, which is the medical term for eating non-nutritive substances. While it might seem like a simple habit, it is frequently your body signaling that your iron stores are depleted. If you find yourself frequently craving ice or other non-food items, it is time to investigate your internal health.

I recommend getting a blood test to check for low iron levels if you notice these behaviors. Addressing the root cause can help resolve these specific cravings and improve your overall well-being. Please consult a qualified medical professional for proper diagnosis and treatment rather than assuming it is just a dietary quirk.

recent_videos.title: Avoid hair oil if you have these problems!
recent_videos.description:
AVOID HAIR OIL IF YOU HAVE THESE 4 CONDITIONS!

Think hair oil is always good for your scalp? Not necessarily!

Excessive oil application may worsen certain skin conditions, including:

1. Dandruff – May worsen flaking and itching.

2. Facial Acne – Can clog pores around your hairline and forehead.

3. Scalp Folliculitis – May aggravate itchy, inflamed bumps around hair follicles.

4. Back Acne – Oil transferred onto your back may contribute to clogged pores and breakouts.

Dermatologist Tip: Hair oil isn’t bad for everyone! But if you’re prone to these conditions, avoid applying it directly to your scalp or leaving it on for too long.

recent_videos.title: Exclusive Interview with Natasha Vora | Founder of Feier #NatashaVora, #Feier #bodysuit #innerwear
recent_videos.description:
Exclusive Interview with Natasha Vora, Founder of Feier, exploring the brand’s journey, design philosophy and approach to contemporary fashion and activewear.

In this exclusive conversation with Fashion Value Chain, Natasha Vora discusses Feier’s brand identity, colour choices, apparel design and the role of innovative fibres and fabrics in creating comfortable, functional and stylish activewear. The discussion explores nylon and performance fabrics for activewear, the design and fit of leggings and bodysuits, sportswear trends, fabric quality, stretch, comfort and durability.

The interview also features a rapid-fire round covering comfort versus style, leggings, activewear essentials, fashion preferences and the evolving relationship between performance and everyday dressing.

Watch the full interview to discover insights into activewear design, fabric innovation and the future of fashion-led performance apparel.

Subscribe to Fashion Value Chain for more exclusive interviews, fashion industry insights and textile innovations. #NatashaVora, #Feier, #ExclusiveInterview, #Activewear, #Leggings, #Bodysuits, #Sportswear, #FashionIndustry

recent_videos.title: Plant-Based Leather Alternatives in Sustainable Fashion
recent_videos.description:
Plant-based leather alternatives are gaining attention across sustainable fashion, with materials derived from sources such as pineapple leaves, cactus and other plant-based or agricultural resources.

But being plant-based does not automatically make a material sustainable. Durability, processing methods, coatings, chemical use and end-of-life options all influence its overall environmental impact.

The Galaxy Z Fold8 brings a 201g foldable design compared to the 254g iPhone Duo, along with a 5.5-inch outer display that unfolds into a 7.6-inch main display.
That extra screen also gives you more room to multitask, with Multiwindow letting you run three apps side by side, compared to a two-way split on iPhone Duo. Switching to Galaxy is simple with Smart Switch via QR, while Quick Share makes sharing files easy.
For group videos, My FanCam lets you capture the whole scene and choose your subject afterwards, while Galaxy AI automatically reframes the footage around them.
And with EMI starting at ₹2,150/month, the Galaxy Z Fold8 makes the foldable experience more accessible. Plus, you can now get the Galaxy Z Fold8 at the price of the Galaxy Z Fold7.
If you’re going foldable, why stop at your first fold?

recent_videos.title: This CEO Faced a $300 Million Decision 💸
recent_videos.description:
At its peak, Blockbuster had over 9,000 stores and dominated the movie-rental industry.

But Netflix offered a different experience: rent DVDs by mail and avoid traditional late fees.

In 2004, Blockbuster CEO John Antioco decided to eliminate late fees to compete. Those fees had contributed around $250–$300 million to annual operating income.

The move was controversial, and Blockbuster struggled to adapt as the industry shifted toward online rentals and streaming.

In 2010, Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy.

A powerful business lesson: never underestimate a competitor changing what customers expect.

#Blockbuster #Netflix #BusinessStrategy #BusinessFailure #MarketingLessons #MubasshirShaikh

recent_videos.title: How Biscoff Went From Luxury to ₹10 👀 #casestudy
recent_videos.description:
Lotus Biscoff started in Belgium in 1932 and became famous worldwide for its caramelised biscuits.

In India, imported Biscoff was known as a premium product. But in 2025, locally manufactured packs launched at an entry price of ₹10 through a partnership with Mondelez.

The strategy makes Biscoff more affordable—but can a luxury image survive mass-market pricing?

This is the branding challenge every business should understand.

#LotusBiscoff #Branding #MarketingStrategy #BusinessCaseStudy #BrandPositioning #MubasshirShaikh

recent_videos.title: This Pillow Was Once a Cigarette Filter 🤯 #startup
recent_videos.description:
Every day, cigarette butts are thrown away as waste. But two Indian brothers saw a business opportunity where others saw garbage.

Naman and Vipul Gupta founded Code Effort in 2018 to recycle cigarette waste into useful products.

The filters are processed into fibre for cushions, pillows and soft toys, while the paper and leftover tobacco are repurposed too.

Their biggest challenge? Collecting enough cigarette butts to keep the business running.

A powerful example of how an environmental problem can inspire an innovative business idea. 🇮🇳

name: Pathbreaker
description:
Pathbreaker is not just a journey across places, people, and inner worlds it is a living, evolving space where soulful conversations, ancient wisdom, and the rhythm of life come together through thoughtful storytelling.

Each season unfolds through real conversations set in meaningful locations across India and beyond, from ancient temples and palaces to cities, communities, and quiet natural landscapes.

Through art, culture, spirituality, health, creativity, and everyday human stories, Pathbreaker explores how we grow as individuals and as a society from movement and identity to awareness, responsibility, joy, and belonging.

This is not a travel show or a podcast. It is a slow, reflective exploration of what it means to be human in the modern world, rooted in lived experience and timeless wisdom.

There are no answers here, only journeys, conversations, and states of being.

Let’s follow wonder and become the friend we seek in the world.

What is **Kundalini Meditation**? How does Osho's Kundalini Meditation work, and what can we learn from its four stages of shaking, dance, silence and Shavasana?

In this in-depth guide, **Ritika Anand (Sannyas name: Mapremjaya)** shares her personal experience and understanding of **Osho's Kundalini Meditation**, Kundalini energy, sensitivity, creative expression and the movement from activity into stillness.

For Ritika, Kundalini Meditation is not simply about physical movement. It is an experiential practice that can open us to deeper layers of the body and consciousness, explore different forms of expression, and create space for creative life-force energy.

She also shares a personal experience of discovering **“the watcher” within**, and what she understood through finding a centre that could remain still even while the body was moving.

recent_videos.title: The Meditation Nobody Talks About | Osho's Nadabrahma Meditation Explained
recent_videos.description:
What if meditation wasn't about stopping your thoughts... but about reconnecting with the whole of existence?

In this in-depth guide, Ritika Anand (Sannyas Name: Mapremjaya) shares her personal understanding and experience of Osho's Nadabrahma Meditation—one of the most beautiful yet least discussed active meditations.

Unlike Dynamic Meditation, Nadabrahma is a gentle, music-led practice built around humming, conscious movement, receiving, sharing and silence. Through consistent practice, it helps us slow the mind, reduce inner noise, reconnect with our body and experience the deeper understanding that we are never separate from the whole.

In this video you'll discover:

• What Nadabrahma Meditation is
• Why humming creates healing vibrations throughout the body
• How sound connects us with nature and existence
• The meaning behind sharing and receiving energy
• Why slowing down is essential for true meditation
• How Nadabrahma supports inner harmony, creativity and presence
• Ritika's personal experience with this beautiful Osho Meditation
• The four stages of Nadabrahma Meditation explained

Whether you're new to meditation, already practising Osho Active Meditations, or simply looking for a deeper connection with yourself and the world around you, this guide offers a practical and experiential understanding of Nadabrahma Meditation.

recent_videos.description:
✨ A simple traditional recipe for your hair and wellness routine!

This easy DIY recipe combines black sesame seeds, kalonji (black seed), and optional honey. Black sesame seeds contain antioxidants, healthy fats, and essential minerals that support overall health.

🤎 Recipe:
• 3 tbsp black sesame seeds
• 3 tbsp kalonji
• 3–4 tbsp honey (optional)

How to make it:

1. Dry roast the black sesame seeds and kalonji.
2. Blend them into a fine powder.
3. Mix in honey if desired.
4. Start with a small amount and see how your body responds.

Basically, loose powder = setting + baking and pressed powder = touch-ups + on-the-go convenience. 💅🏻

recent_videos.title: Makeup fixer vs setting spray ⁉️
recent_videos.description:
Girlies, ek important makeup tip jo har beginner ko pata honi chahiye! 🎀✨ Har setting spray ko makeup ke beech use karna zaroori nahi hota. 💗

Some sprays are mainly designed to help your makeup last longer, while others can be used for prep, refreshing or between makeup steps. But remember, setting spray aur fixing spray ki terminology har brand mein same nahi hoti, so product ke instructions check karna is important!

For example, L’Oréal Infallible 3-Second Setting Mist is marketed for long-lasting makeup, and its instructions recommend applying it once your makeup is complete and dry. So, if you want to use a spray between layers, choose one whose brand instructions allow that use.

✨ How to use a makeup spray correctly:
• Apply and blend your base in thin layers.
• If your spray is suitable for between-step use, mist lightly.
• Let the mist settle and dry before applying the next product.
• Avoid blending over a base that’s still visibly wet.
• Film-forming ingredients can help improve makeup wear, while a fine mist may help reduce that overly powdery look.

And girlies, you don’t need to buy multiple sprays just because they’re labelled differently. Choose according to your skin, desired finish and the product’s actual instructions! 💅🏻

recent_videos.title: Don’t Throw Away Old Shoes & Clothes! Donate Them to GreenSole Foundation ♻️ #sustainableliving
recent_videos.description:
Have old shoes, slippers or clothes lying unused at home? 👟👕 Give them a second life with GreenSole Foundation!

GreenSole Foundation accepts old footwear and clothes for upcycling, helping turn items that might otherwise go to waste into something useful.

💚 HOW TO DONATE YOUR OLD SHOES & CLOTHES

📍 Option 1: Visit a drop-off centre

Centres are available in Mumbai, Delhi, Pune, Surat, Bhavnagar, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Udaipur, Nouvamundi, Haryana and Kolkata.

Visit https://greensolefoundation.com to find your nearest drop-off centre and confirm its exact address.

👟 What footwear can you donate?
Usable old shoes, slippers and other footwear.

Please avoid sports-stud shoes, heels, footwear with broken soles, and children’s footwear for children under 5.

👕 What clothes can you donate?
Clean, wearable clothes.

Please avoid deeply stained or torn clothes, infant clothes and lingerie.

📦 Option 2: Courier your donations

Don’t have a drop-off centre nearby? You can courier your old footwear and clothes directly to GreenSole Foundation for upcycling.

Courier address:

GreenSole Foundation
A-460, C/o Ram Fashion Exports,
TTC Industrial Area, MIDC, Mahape,
Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra 400701, India.

🌿 Before buying more, look at what you already own. Donate responsibly and help give usable items a second life.

In this Short, I’m sharing a glimpse of how I compost kitchen waste at home. Yes, things like vegetable and fruit scraps, eggshells, tea leaves and other compostable kitchen waste can be composted at home.

The key is BALANCE. Layer your kitchen waste with brown leaves, cocopeat or other carbon-rich materials like brown paper and cardboard. Keep building these layers to maintain airflow and aeration, turn the pile about once a week, and give it time to break down.

With the right conditions, your compost can be ready in around 45 days. 🌿

recent_videos.title: Don’t Pour Used Cooking  Oil Down the Drain! ♻️ Here’s What to Do Instead
recent_videos.description:
Enjoying pakoras, samosas and all your favourite fried food this monsoon? 🌧️🍟 Please don’t pour the used cooking oil down the drain.

Here’s what you can do instead:

🫙 Let the oil cool, strain it if needed, and store it in a bottle.

🪔 Have a small quantity left? You can use a small amount to light diyas outside your home during festivals or celebrations.

♻️ Have more oil left? Recycle it.
Call 1800 890 3841 to contact the Ecoil team. Where the service is available, they can arrange a doorstep pickup, and you can also get paid per litre for your used cooking oil.

Why should you recycle used cooking oil?

When oil is poured down the drain, it can:

• Clog pipes and drains
• Pollute rivers and other water bodies
• Make wastewater treatment more difficult and expensive
• Harm aquatic life
• Waste a valuable resource that can be converted into biodiesel

Used cooking oil can be repurposed as a feedstock for biodiesel. FSSAI’s RUCO (Repurpose Used Cooking Oil) initiative was created to facilitate the collection and conversion of used cooking oil into biodiesel and other useful products. 

India’s National Policy on Biofuels has an indicative target of 5% biodiesel blending in diesel by 2030, with used cooking oil among the feedstocks identified for biofuel production. 

✨ What if you’ve only used a little oil?

If you’ve lightly stir-fried or pan-fried something, wipe the pan with a compostable bamboo tissue or paper towel before washing it.

• If there’s only a tiny amount of oil on the tissue and it’s compostable, you can add it to your compost.
• If the tissue is heavily soaked with oil, dispose of it in your dry waste bin.

Small actions in every kitchen can create a huge impact across India. 🇮🇳♻️

Save this video and share it with someone who still pours cooking oil down the sink!

recent_videos.title: Vegan Cheese Is Evolving Beyond Plant-Based Alternatives 🧀 #Dairy #cruelty #innovation
recent_videos.description:
vegan cheese company just got discontinued, and it's the best news in food this year.
Formo sold 300,000+ units of its cow-free cream cheese across 3,500 German supermarkets, reaching over 125,000 shoppers. Then it shut the brand down in 2025 because the point was never the cheese. It was proof that ordinary people would buy it.
Now they're selling the protein itself to the food industry, and they debuted it at IFT FIRST in Chicago this month, the trade show where food brands source their ingredients.
And it matters, because a cow only makes milk after she's had a calf. So she's made pregnant, again and again, and her calf is taken from her within hours of birth so we can have what was meant for him.
Most people never picture that part. They just picture cheese.
This protein doesn't need any of it. Same melt, same stretch, no mother, no calf, no separation.
I think that's the better version of change, not asking everyone to switch brands, but changing what's inside the ones they already reach for.

recent_videos.title: If you eat eggs, this is something you must know. #plantbased #sustainablesolutions #sustainability
recent_videos.description:
If you eat eggs, this is something you must know.
Every year, around 7 billion male chicks are killed within hours of hatching. That's about 200 every second, simply because they were born male and will never lay eggs. It happens in free-range and organic farms too.
Their sisters don't have it easier. Hens have been bred to lay around 300 eggs a year, and in a battery cage, each hen spends her whole life in less space than an A4 sheet of paper.
But that cruelty is avoidable.
There is something new on shelves at Walmart and Target now. It is called OvoPro by @theeverycompany, an egg white protein made by yeast instead of a hen. This means no cage, no hatchery, and no killing of male chicks.
For almost everything on our plate today, a kinder version already exists. Tofu scramble instead of an omelette.
Chickpea flour omelet for breakfast. Flax or aquafaba in your baking. And now, egg protein without the hen.
We don't have to be perfect. We just have to start switching, one meal at a time. Imagine the world that adds up to.
If there's a kinder way to eat the same food, what's really stopping us? Tell us below.

recent_videos.title: Balenciaga has put up silk on the runway without harming a single silk worm #luxary #sustainability
recent_videos.description:
The new status symbol isn't the logo. It's the material, especially when it's clever enough to be kind.
@balenciaga  recently showed a couture gown made with silk that never came from a silkworm.
The silk protein comes from @amsilk , a German biotech company that produces it using microbes in a process that's a little like brewing. That protein is then spun into thread and woven much like conventional silk.
The interesting part? There's no cocoon involved.
Conventional silk is made by boiling the cocoon with the silkworm still inside, so the continuous thread can be extracted without breaking. This version skips the cocoon altogether.
And the resulting material is biodegradable, without leaving microplastics behind.
Balenciaga fittingly called the piece the Cocoon Gown.
It's a pretty fascinating shift in what craftsmanship can mean. Because the future of luxury might not only be about what a designer can do with a fabric, but what we can rethink at the level of the material itself.
When the houses that define luxury start experimenting with materials like this, sustainability starts looking less like a compromise and more like the next frontier of design.
Save this for the next time someone says sustainable materials can't be luxurious.

recent_videos.title: Your vanity might be full of things that once had a heartbeat. #crueltyfree #compassion
recent_videos.description:
We’re used to thinking of animal-derived materials as something obvious: leather, fur, wool. But some of them are hiding in plain sight, disguised as luxury, beauty, or something simply pretty like the red coral in jewellery, pearls, shells, mother-of-pearl.

And coral is a particularly strange one to think about. What looks like a beautiful red stone is actually the skeleton of a colony of tiny animals.

Sadly, we've normalized turning something that was once alive into something for our use. 

It's about time we actually know what we're looking at.

Because once you know, you can start asking a different question when you buy something beautiful: What had to die for this to exist?

And sometimes, the answer is nothing. Because plantbased and synthetic materials can replace animal-derived ones.

Recycled materials can become jewellery, and some alternatives can even support restoration instead of extraction.

Beauty doesn't have to come at the expense of another life.

recent_videos.title: A T-rex just became a handbag.
recent_videos.description:
No animal was harmed to make it. There are none left to harm.

And that’s almost the point. Every other animal we’ve turned into leather had to die for it. But back in April, a bio-tech company, Lab-Grown Leather, worked with @VMLglobal and The Organoid Company to create something different.

They took fragment took fragments of fossilised T. rex collagen, used AI to rebuild the rest, and grew real leather from living cells. Designer @enfinleve shaped it into the bag. No herd. No slaughter. No hide.

For as long as we can remember, leather has meant loss. This is the first real proof it doesn’t have to.

If a bag can be grown instead of killed for, what else have we been told there was no other way to make?

Save this for the next time someone says cruelty-free can’t be the future.

recent_videos.description:
✨ The RIGHT way to drape a beautiful border saree! 🥻💕

Do you also drape your border saree like this? 👀
If you do, the beautiful border can lose its charm and the overall saree look may not appear as neat as it should. ❌

Try this easy pallu draping technique instead! 👇✨

🥻 Step-by-Step

1️⃣ Half-fold the pallu
2️⃣ Hold the saree border and start making pleats
3️⃣ Keep the pleats slightly shorter than the border
4️⃣ Open both borders at the front
5️⃣ Secure the pleats from the back with a safety pin
6️⃣ Continue the technique along the pallu to your desired length
7️⃣ Place the pallu over your shoulder and pin it securely
8️⃣ Gently arrange the front pleats ✨

And there you have it! 😍

A neat and elegant pallu with the beautiful saree border properly highlighted. ❤️

❌ Stop Pinning Your Pallu Like This!

Instead, try this simple 2-pin saree pallu hack! 👇🏻✨

If your pallu keeps slipping or you struggle to pin it neatly with a close-back blouse, this technique can help you get a cleaner and more secure drape.

👗 Step-by-Step

Step 1: Drape your saree pallu neatly over your shoulder.
Step 2: ❌ Don’t force the pin through the middle of the pallu.
Step 3: Take a small safety pin.
Step 4: Attach it to the front side of the pallu near the shoulder.
Step 5: Take a second safety pin.
Step 6: Fix it to the edge of the blouse at the side/back.
Step 7: Adjust the fall of the pallu. Done! ✔️

✨ Less slipping

recent_videos.title: పిల్లల కోసం పిల్లకలువలు 🌿 | Cotton to Cloth Workshop | Kids Learn Traditional Crafts | Telugu Pulse
recent_videos.description:
పిల్లలు మనం రోజూ ఉపయోగించే వస్తువుల వెనుక ఉన్న శ్రమను అర్థం చేసుకుంటున్నారా? 👧🏻🌿

మన ఒంటిపై ఉన్న బట్ట పత్తి నుంచి ఎలా తయారవుతుంది? నూలు ఎలా తీస్తారు? వస్త్రాన్ని ఎలా నేస్తారు? ప్రకృతిలో లభించే పదార్థాలతో సహజ రంగులు ఎలా తయారుచేస్తారు?

ఈ వీడియోలో పిల్లకలువలు నిర్వహించిన **Cotton to Cloth Workshop** ద్వారా పిల్లలు పత్తిని పరిచయం చేసుకోవడం నుంచి నూలు తీయడం, నేయడం, సహజ రంగులతో Tie & Dye చేయడం వరకు వివిధ దశలను స్వయంగా ప్రయత్నించి తెలుసుకున్న అనుభవాన్ని మీ ముందుకు తీసుకొస్తున్నాం.

ఈ కార్యక్రమం వెనుక ఉన్న ఉద్దేశం ఏంటి? ప్రకృతికి, సంప్రదాయాలకు, స్థానిక వృత్తులకు పిల్లలను దగ్గర చేయడం ఎందుకు ముఖ్యం? పిల్లకలువలు నిర్వహించే Earth Dialogues, Natural Building, Farming వంటి కార్యక్రమాల లక్ష్యం ఏంటి?

ఈ విషయాలను పిల్లల అనుభవాలు, తల్లిదండ్రుల అభిప్రాయాలు, నిర్వాహకుల మాటల ద్వారా తెలుసుకుందాం.

🌿 **పిల్లకలువలు వర్క్‌షాప్ వివరాల కోసం:**

📞 +91 82472 88854  
📞 +91 97010 59469

వర్క్‌షాప్ ఫీజు, తేదీలు, రిజిస్ట్రేషన్ వివరాల కోసం పై నంబర్లకు కాల్ చేయండి.

మన పిల్లలకు విషయాలను చెప్పడం మాత్రమే కాదు… వాటిని స్వయంగా అనుభవించి నేర్చుకునే అవకాశం కూడా ఇద్దాం.

మీకు ఈ కథ నచ్చితే వీడియోను Like చేయండి, మీ అభిప్రాయాన్ని Comment చేయండి, ఇలాంటి మరిన్ని నిజమైన కథల కోసం Telugu Pulse ఛానల్‌ను Subscribe చేయండి.

**తెలుగు పల్స్ — మన నేల… మన మనుషులు… మన స్వరం.**

The business lesson A strong legacy isn't built overnight it's built through generations of hard work 🏏

Its FY2025 annual report recorded approximately ₹502 crore in revenue.

The business lesson You don't always need a revolutionary product to build a successful company. Sometimes, making an everyday product better and more accessible can create a massive opportunity. 🇮🇳

How did a simple rose based drink become one of India's most iconic brands ❤️

Rooh Afza isn't just a summer drink it's a part of India's food and cultural history From its beginnings under Hamdard Laboratories to becoming a familiar name across generations Rooh Afza has managed to stay relevant for more than a century.

The story goes back to 1906 when Hakim Abdul Majeed founded Hamdard in Delhi. What started as a traditional Unani medicine venture eventually created products that became household names, with Rooh Afza becoming its most recognizable drink.

From Rooh Afza milkshakes and sherbets to its presence during Ramadan and Indian summers the brand became much more than a beverage Its distinctive red colour rose based flavour and nostalgic identity helped it build a connection that lasted across generations.

But the real business lesson is even more interesting how do you keep a century old Indian brand relevant while consumer tastes keep changing

That's what makes the Rooh Afza story worth studying. 🇮🇳

recent_videos.title: SUTA Founders at UID | Sujata & Taniya Biswas on Fashion, Handlooms & Entrepreneurship
recent_videos.description:
What does it take to turn a love for Indian textiles into a fashion brand with a story of its own? ✨

Unitedworld Institute of Design (UID), Ahmedabad, welcomed **Sujata and Taniya Biswas, co-founders of SUTA**, for an interactive session with students and faculty.

From their journey of building a fashion label to the stories woven into every fabric, the session explored the intersection of creativity, entrepreneurship, and India's rich handloom heritage.

Key insights from the conversation included:
- Reviving Indian handlooms for the modern wearer
- Building a sustainable fashion brand
- Storytelling through textiles and design
- Navigating the business of fashion as designers

An inspiring exchange of ideas for the next generation of designers, reminding us that great design goes beyond aesthetics — it carries culture, purpose, and stories.

recent_videos.title: Gen Zs take on National Handloom Day at UID-NCR!
recent_videos.description:
National Handloom Day is celebrated to commemorate the Swadeshi Movement, launched on this day in 1905. This defining moment encouraged Indians to embrace indigenous products and celebrate the country's rich weaving traditions. While we know the history and significance of this movement, an equally important question remains: what does handloom mean to Gen Z today?

For a generation driven by individuality, sustainability, and conscious consumption, handlooms represent more than just heritage. They are a blend of craftsmanship, culture, and contemporary style. But how do young people truly perceive them? Do they see handloom as a timeless fashion statement, a sustainable lifestyle choice, or simply a part of India's cultural legacy?

This National Handloom Day, let's move beyond the history books and hear directly from Gen Z about their perspectives, preferences, and the future they envision for India's handloom heritage.

Music Credit: Vaishnav Jan by Abhinav Parmar
